headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Airbyte’s broad egress can feed AutoGPT’s shell/filesystem workflows, creating unsafe default data movement and actioning.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte exposes API-based data movement and broad network egress, while AutoGPT can execute shell commands and read/write the filesystem. A prompt-injection path is plausible only if Airbyte outputs are manually or programmatically fed into AutoGPT as instructions; no shared channel is documented, so this stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is copied into AutoGPT prompts or files without sanitization, instruction hijacking becomes possible.
IF a shared workspace or message bridge is added between the agents, the injection surface expands.
mitigations: Keep Airbyte outputs out of AutoGPT prompt text.
Use a strict schema/JSON parser for any handoff files.
Disable automatic file-watching between the agents.
Add a human review step before AutoGPT consumes Airbyte-generated content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; AutoGPT can access the filesystem and has allowlisted egress. If they share a workspace or handoff files, sensitive business data can flow from Airbyte into AutoGPT and then out through its network path. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible in default-style integrations, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF Airbyte writes business data into files that AutoGPT reads, leakage risk is present.
IF AutoGPT is configured to transmit file contents to external services, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces.
Redact or tokenize business data before handoff.
Restrict AutoGPT to a minimal allowlist of destinations.
Turn off automatic ingestion of shared files.
Audit outbound requests for any file-content uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can move data over the network and AutoGPT can write files and spawn subprocesses. Their capabilities overlap on mutable data flows, so concurrent writes or conflicting updates are plausible if they share a directory or pipeline state. AutoGPT’s lack of multi-instance support increases coordination risk; Airbyte’s profile does not show locking.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or pipeline artifact, conflicts can occur.
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking, race conditions become more likely.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Run only one AutoGPT instance per shared resource.
Use immutable handoff artifacts instead of in-place edits.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data that AutoGPT may treat as input for shell or subprocess actions. Because AutoGPT can execute commands and spawn subprocesses, an erroneous Airbyte output can cascade into irreversible downstream actions if consumed without verification. This is a default-danger pattern when data pipelines feed autonomous action agents.
conditions: IF AutoGPT uses Airbyte-produced records as authoritative inputs, downstream actions can be wrong at scale.
IF AutoGPT is allowed to act without a verification gate, cascading errors can reach external systems.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Airbyte and AutoGPT.
Require human approval for any action derived from pipeline output.
Limit AutoGPT to read-only analysis mode for Airbyte data.
Log and diff all proposed actions before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte explicitly touches business data, while AutoGPT’s profile does not indicate regulated data classes or residency constraints. The pair does not show a documented compliance mismatch, but if business data includes regulated records and AutoGPT is deployed in a different jurisdiction or retention regime, a gap could emerge. Only Airbyte is cited because the compliance concern is data-class driven here.
conditions: IF business data includes regulated personal data, residency or retention obligations may apply.
IF AutoGPT stores or forwards the same data under a different policy, compliance gaps appear.
mitigations: Classify the business data before routing it to AutoGPT.
Block regulated records from the handoff path.
Set a short retention window for shared artifacts.
Document the processing location and retention policy.
